articles.summary:

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suarez for his 100th goal in 115 appearances across all competitions with Miami.
The milestone came against the same club Messi scored his first Inter Miami goal against. He scored on a stoppage-time free kick to beat Cruz Azul 2-1 in his Miami debut in July 2023.
Casemiro made it 2-0 in the 81st minute, heading in a corner from Messi.
The Brazilian midfielder has scored four goals, all headers, in his last five matches after scoring in three consecutive games against CF Montreal, Atlanta United and Chicago before being held scoreless Saturday against Nashville.
The victory gave Inter Miami another trophy three years after Messi's arrival. Miami won the Leagues Cup in 2023, the Supporters' Shield in 2024 and MLS Cup in 2025.

articles.title: Meet Kremer, World Bank's new chief economist
articles.summary: The World Bank on Wednesday named Nobel laureate and University of Chicago professor Michael Kremer as its next chief economist, succeeding Indermit Gill, who retired last month.Kremer, 61, won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences in 2019 jointly with Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee for their experimental approach to alleviating global poverty.He will take charge on October 1, shortly before the annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Bangkok, Thailand. He is the first economist to join the World Bank as chief economist with a Nobel Prize already in hand; former chief economists Joseph Stiglitz and Paul Romer received the Nobel after their tenures at the bank.Also read: World Bank names Nobel laureate Michael Kremer as next chief economistWho is Michael Kremer?Born on November 12, 1964, in New York, Kremer is an economist known for applying experimental methods to development problems, particularly in areas such as education, healthcare, agriculture and access to finance. He earned his doctorate in economics from Harvard University in 1992 and then worked at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.He then become a Harvard professor in 1999.Kremer is currently a University Professor in Economics at the University of Chicago, where he also directs the Development Innovation Lab (DIL). The lab develops and scales innovations in areas including agriculture, education, water treatment, road safety and microfinance, with the stated potential to reach more than 100 million people in low- and middle-income countries.Over the years, Kremer has worked on breaking down the broad challenge of global poverty into smaller, testable questions and using field experiments to determine which interventions work.Kremer's Nobel PrizeThe Nobel Committee recognised Kremer, Duflo and Banerjee in 2019 for introducing an experimental approach that transformed development economics. Since the mid-1990s, the economists have used field experiments to test interventions aimed at improving educational outcomes and child health, among other areas.The scientific approach has also involved testing programmes in real-world settings before examining whether they can be expanded. This allowed Kremer and his collaborators to connect academic research with programmes affecting millions of people.From vaccines to deworming programmesOne of Kremer's notable contributions has been his work on Advance Market Commitments, a mechanism in which donors commit funding to encourage pharmaceutical companies to develop and produce vaccines for low-income countries.According to ADB Food Systems, Kremer helped design an Advance Market Commitment for a pneumococcal vaccine. The initiative resulted in three approved vaccines being rolled out across 60 countries, with an estimated 700,000 lives saved.His research on deworming among schoolchildren also had implications for education and public health policy. The research examined whether treating children for parasitic worm infections could improve school attendance.The findings helped inform large-scale deworming programmes, with governments in Africa and South Asia providing about 2 billion treatments since 2014, according to the World Bank.His work has also extended to water safety.ADB Food Systems mentioned that Kremer's water-related work reaches about 9 million people through Evidence Action, while his broader research portfolio includes agriculture, education and finance.Technology and developmentKremer has also focused on how technology can address development challenges. At the University of Chicago, his Development Innovation Lab works on scaling innovations across several sectors in developing economies.He is also a co-founder of Precision Development, which uses digital technology to provide smallholder farmers with information intended to improve productivity and incomes. His work includes AI-based agricultural weather forecasting and the Human-Centered Weather Forecasts initiative.Kremer has also been involved in the Development Innovation Ventures (DIV), a fund administered by the US Agency for International Development that he co-founded in 2010. The fund was later shut down after Donald Trump returned to the White House in 2025.His research has therefore combined experimental economics with an emphasis on taking successful interventions beyond pilot projects and into large-scale programmes.What are Kremer's views on global development landscape?Kremer's appointment as the next World Bank chief economist comes as the organisation faces a crucial development landscape marked by financing pressures and the need to generate jobs and improve living standards in developing economies.In a 2024 keynote at a World Bank event titled "The Great Incoherence: Growth and Human Development in an Era of Stagnation", Kremer called for reforms to help countries meet ambitious development goals. He highlighted funding innovative pilot projects and creating incentives for research into new technologies as key themes.The emphasis on innovation and scaling is also reflected in his work at the University of Chicago. In announcing his appointment, World Bank President Ajay Banga said Kremer had spent his career identifying what works in development and proving it at scale.Kremer, in a statement, said the World Bank has significant research capacity to develop and test innovative solutions to development problems, as well as the operational reach to scale them up. He also pointed to new technologies as an opportunity to boost growth amid the major challenges facing the global economy.His career combines academic economics, field experimentation and policy implementation, experience that will now move to the World Bank, where he is set to become chief economist from October 1.

articles.summary:
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a proposal to raise the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) to Rs 25,000 per month from Rs 15,000.
The wage ceiling revision is taking place after 12 years.
The decision is expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees within the ambit of mandatory EPFO coverage, significantly widening social security protection for workers, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said at a press briefing.
The EPFO wage ceiling remained unchanged from 2004 to 2014 and was enhanced to Rs 15,000 in September 2014.
The present decision carries forward this approach by further raising the ceiling to Rs 25,000 to reflect sustained wage growth, rising incomes and continued expansion of formal employment over the intervening years, an official release said.

articles.title: BIS raises gold hallmarking fee to ₹75 from ₹45 ahead of festive season
articles.summary:
The Bureau of Indian Standards has revised hallmarking charges for gold and silver articles, raising the fee for gold to Rs 75 from Rs 45, while retaining the charge for silver at Rs 35, with immediate effect ahead of the festive season.
The increase has been notified through the BIS (Hallmarking) Amendment Regulations, 2026, dated September 14, 2026.
Under the amended Schedule IV, jewellers are required to pay a hallmarking fee of Rs 75 per article, subject to a minimum charge of Rs 200 per consignment, while for silver articles, the fee payable by jewellers to recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs) is fixed at Rs 35 per article, with a minimum of Rs 150 per consignment.
BIS hallmarking verifies the purity of a precious metal used in jewellery and certifies the article under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), containing the three key markings: its logo, Karat or millesimal fineness, and a six-digit alphanumeric code known as the Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID)

articles.title: EU chief von der Leyen proposes ban on social media for children under 13
articles.summary:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed banning children under 13 from accessing social media, online games and chatbots on Wednesday during her annual State of the European Union speech in Strasbourg.
"I am aware that many perceive the power of Big Tech as overwhelming and impossible to roll back. I disagree," said the EU executive.
"We do not have to accept addictive features. We do not have to accept children being drawn into ever more extreme content. We do not have to accept that girls have their photos used for AI-generated sexualized images," she said.
Von der Leyen said that under her proposal "mini accounts" chaperoned by guardians would be granted to kids aged 13-15.
The EU's 27 member nations will now vote on the proposal, which could spark tensions with US President Donald Trump, who has long criticized Europe's tech regulations.
